title: La visite surprise de Catherine  (Catherine's Surprise Visit)

segments.t: At the agency, Noemie receives a shock when Mathias's estranged wife Catherine arrives asking to see her. Terrified that Catherine has discovered their secret affair, Noemie scrambles for an excuse to flee the office. Listen to the scene in French first.
Catherine Barneville veut me voir?
Dites-lui que Mathias est sorti.
Dites que j'ai un travail urgent.
Mathias? C'est Noémie.
Ta femme est là à l'agence!
Elle est au courant pour nous?
Je ne sais pas quoi faire, rappelle-moi!
Bonjour, Noémie.
Bonjour Catherine. Désolée, je dois partir.
Attends, c'est à propos de Mathias.
Je suis très en retard.
Je déjeune avec Camille et sa mère.
Camille et sa mère?
J'ai besoin de manger un steak tartare.
Je viens avec toi!
D'accord... allons-y ensemble.
Let's examine how Noemie scrambles to hide her secret affair with Mathias.
Catherine Barneville veut me voir?
'Catherine Barneville wants to see me?' Notice 'me' sits before 'to see' rather than after 'wants', turning surprise into a question through pitch alone.
Dites-lui que Mathias est sorti.
'Tell her that Mathias went out.' Joining 'to her' with a hyphen onto polite 'tell' covers both 'tell him' and 'tell her'—context tells you which one in French.
Dites que j'ai un travail urgent.
'Say that I have urgent work.' Uncountable 'work' in English becomes 'an urgent job' here, with the cognate 'urgent' following 'work' in French.
Mathias? C'est Noémie.
'Mathias? It's Noemie.' Phone callers in French identify themselves with 'it is' plus their name rather than 'this is'.
Ta femme est là à l'agence!
'Your wife is here at the agency!' One everyday French word covers both 'woman' and 'wife'; pairing it with 'your' makes 'your wife' unmistakable.
Elle est au courant pour nous?
'Does she know about us?' Literally 'at the current', this handy idiom means 'in the loop' or 'informed about something' in French.
Je ne sais pas quoi faire, rappelle-moi!
'I don't know what to do, call me back!' After 'know not', speakers switch to stressed 'what' before 'to do' in French, then tuck 'me' onto 'call back' with a hyphen.
Bonjour, Noémie.
'Hello, Noemie.' Addressing Mathias's assistant by her first name after a calm 'good day' sounds polite on the surface yet pointed in French.
Bonjour Catherine. Désolée, je dois partir.
'Hello Catherine. Sorry, I have to leave.' Clipped down to a single word, 'sorry' gains a silent '-e' in writing for Noemie, followed by 'I must leave' in French.
Attends, c'est à propos de Mathias.
'Wait, it's about Mathias.' Built around a cognate of 'purpose', that three-word connector means 'about' or 'concerning' in French.
Je suis très en retard.
'I am running very late.' Sliding 'very' right ahead of the 'in delay' chunk intensifies 'I am late' without needing 'running' in French.
Je déjeune avec Camille et sa mère.
'I'm having lunch with Camille and her mother.' Simple present 'I lunch' covers an imminent plan just like 'I'm having lunch' in English, while 'her' matches 'mother'.
Camille et sa mère?
'Camille and her mother?' Echoing those four words with rising pitch asks for confirmation, while 'his' and 'her' share the exact same form before 'mother' in French.
J'ai besoin de manger un steak tartare.
'I need to eat a steak tartare.' Famous bistro classic 'steak tartare' puts 'tartare' after 'steak' in French, introduced by 'have need of' plus 'to eat'.
Je viens avec toi!
'I'm coming with you!' Using present 'I come' for an on-the-spot decision sounds immediate and unstoppable in French, paired with stressed 'you' after 'with'.
D'accord... allons-y ensemble.

'All right... let's go together.' Adding '-y'—meaning 'there'—onto 'let us go' gives you a handy chunk you'll hear everywhere for 'let's go!'. Now let's hear the awkward confrontation once more at normal pace.
Catherine Barneville veut me voir?
Dites-lui que Mathias est sorti.
Dites que j'ai un travail urgent.
Mathias? C'est Noémie.
Ta femme est là à l'agence!
Elle est au courant pour nous?
Je ne sais pas quoi faire, rappelle-moi!
Bonjour, Noémie.
Bonjour Catherine. Désolée, je dois partir.
Attends, c'est à propos de Mathias.
Je suis très en retard.
Je déjeune avec Camille et sa mère.
Camille et sa mère?
J'ai besoin de manger un steak tartare.
Je viens avec toi!
D'accord... allons-y ensemble.

Trapped by her own excuse, Noemie now has to escort Mathias's wife to the very restaurant where Mathias's secret daughter and former lover are waiting. Listen to the entire conversation once more in French. See you next time!
À demain!
